free_tier.stated: Be first in line when the beta opens. No spam, ever. No price, plan or allowance is published.

interface_detail: One small agent dials out; the page names no CLI, API or configuration format.
tooling: A Windows app and a single binary are promised; neither is downloadable from the page read.
chaining: Would sit between a home service and friends' clients; with no launched product it composes with nothing yet.

limits.value: beta waitlist; no account can be created yet

binding_note: There is no product to measure: the gate is the closed beta, and no quota can fail before it opens. The page also offers no UDP path, so the ingress verdict holds independently of when the beta opens.

identity_cost.detail: Joining the waitlist requires an email address; the page promises no spam.

reliability_note: Not operating; nothing can be said about reliability.
confidence_note: A launch and a pricing page would settle it; until then only the marketing description exists.

evidence.proved: Pre-beta waitlist page: private relay for services at home, one outbound agent, generic TCP, no ports; no price, no plan, no allowance.

notes: Recorded because a 2026 reader will meet the name in launch feeds. Its pitch, a private relay with nothing exposed to the open internet, is the same shape as Twingate and Border0, not a public UDP ingress.

extras.wg_detail: The product page offers generic TCP behind a private relay and names no UDP forwarding and no WireGuard configuration.
